title: Aubergine and Tomato Curry
subtitle: A rich South Asian curry of soft aubergine in spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Aubergine absorbs spiced sauces beautifully and becomes silky when cooked long enough. This is a straightforward curry that works as a main dish with rice or as a side with grilled meat.
sourceNotes: Aubergine curries appear across India and Sri Lanka under different names. This version draws on the brinjal bhaji tradition of South India.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze for up to 3 months. The aubergine softens further on reheating, which is fine.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half. It reheats well in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day once the spices have had time to develop.

content.text: Salting the aubergine before cooking is optional here because it goes into a long-simmered sauce. Skip it if you are in a hurry. The texture will be slightly firmer but the flavour is the same.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Fry the aubergine in two batches for 4 to 5 minutes per batch until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until they pop. Add the onion and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the ground spices (except garam masala). Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking them down, until the sauce is thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Return the aubergine to the pan. Pour in the coconut milk and 100ml of water. Simmer for 15 minutes until the aubergine is completely tender.
Stir in the garam masala. Season with salt. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice or flatbreads.

items.symptom: The aubergine is spongy and has absorbed too much oil.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough before adding the aubergine.
items.fix: Always fry aubergine in very hot oil so it seals quickly.

items.cause: The spices were burnt in the pan before liquids were added.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the pan to stop burning if it looks dry.

items.cause: The coconut milk was added before the tomatoes had reduced.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes to concentrate the sauce.
